paragraphs: Hyman describes him as a student of Rav, as in Pesachim 105. Rav Hananya and Rav Shelamya and students of Rav were sitting at a meal, and Rav Hamnuna the Elder was standing over them — Rav Amram said to them: "Thus said Rav."
Hyman writes: And so we always find "Rav Amram said Rav," as in Moed Katan 19; Yevamot 34, Nedarim 28, Sotah 12b, 18, Bava Batra 164b; Sanhedrin 104b; Avodah Zarah 19, Bekhorot 26b.
And he also received [teachings] from Rav Assi, as in Eruvin 102a, where Rami bar Yehezkel sent to Rav Amram: "Let the master tell us those fine matters that you told us in the name of Rav Assi."
And in the Jerusalem Talmud, Makkot ch. 1, halakha 5: R' Ba bar Mamal, Rav Amram; Rav Matna said Rav.

Hyman writes: And in the days of Rav Nahman he was already very old, as in Bekhorot 26b [supplied; consulted passage at 27a–27b]: R-N, Rav Amram and Rami bar Hama were traveling in a boat; Rav Amram went up to relieve himself. A woman came and asked them [a question]. Rami bar Hama said to R-N: "Should the master not take account of the elder’s opinion?" And in Bava Batra 162a R-N said to Rav Amram: "From where do you have this?" Those who say [teachings] in his name that we find: Rav Idi bar Avin (first) said Rav Amram, as in Berakhot 49b; Shevuot 11b, 21b.

Hyman further reports: Rav Hiyya bar Avin said Rav Amram, as in Yevamot 25b; Bekhorot 18, and in Ketubot 11b. R-Ch bar Avin said to R-N: "Is it possible that Rav Amram, and all the great ones of the generation, were sitting when Rav Sheshet said this tradition, etc.?"
